title: First-person werewolf brawler in Godot with Claude Code
author: 8paindev
selftext:
Midnight Meats: beat a werewolf through the walls of her own house party. Free demo

Where I used AI:

1. Claude Code wrote all the code + Blender scripts that make lots of the props and all the broken furniture and character model pipeline.

2. Tripo made the bodies, the van and some props.

3. Gemini made concept art and the logo.

4. ElevenLabs made only the news report voices.

5. Suno made the songs.

Free demo : [Midnight Meats by 8painDev](https://8paindev.itch.io/midnight-meats)

comments.author: Plus_Combination_553
comments.body: Thanks for listing exactly where you used AI, tool by tool. That kind of transparency makes the workflow useful for others, and it answers the "is it all AI?" question before anyone asks. The checkered floor and warm kitchen lighting in your screenshot give the scene a strong retro look. Since Claude Code wrote the code and Blender scripts: how much did you have to steer it on the first-person movement and combat feel? Those are usually the parts that need the most iteration. Which of the five tools saved you the most time?

replies.author: 8paindev
replies.body:
Biggest time saver: Claude Code, by far.  
Movement was easy and combat took a lot of steering. I play every step and tell Claude what feels wrong, since it can't feel the game. Hit-stop, shake and punch. the timing all came from that.   
but the first-person hands are still the weak part, so next I'm filming my own punches from eye level and matching the animations to that frame by frame.
